chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys a sale in which there is a measure or weight, he measures/weighs it, then takes it according to what is in it. He said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no objection to it / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy goods measured by weight or volume and then take them after measuring?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a sale involving goods measured by volume or weight is valid provided the buyer takes possession of the specific quantity purchased, thereby resolving concerns regarding *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that commercial transactions are permissible as long as the essential elements of the commodity are clearly defined and transferred, preventing disputes over quantity. It highlights the practical application of removing ambiguity in trade, ensuring that the 'defect' of uncertainty does not invalidate the contract when the goods are tangible and measurable.
